title: Word Break
hints: split wordDict on spaces into a set first, so checking whether a chunk is a valid word is fast
define breakable(i) as: can the first i characters of s be fully decomposed into dictionary words? what is breakable(0), the empty prefix?
breakable(i) is true if there's some earlier valid split point j < i such that breakable(j) is true and s[j:i] is itself a dictionary word
for each i from 1 to n, scan all earlier j where breakable(j) is true and check whether s[j:i] is in the dictionary - the final answer is breakable(n)
commonMistakes: greedily matching the longest or first dictionary word found at each position instead of exploring all valid split points
re-scanning the dictionary as a list on every check instead of using a set, which turns a fast solution slow
forgetting the base case breakable(0) = true, which is what allows the very first word in the split to be recognized

content.problemStatement:
You're given a string `s` and a dictionary of words (given here as a single space-delimited string, `wordDict`).

**Determine whether `s` can be split into a sequence of one or more dictionary words placed back to back.**

The same dictionary word may be reused as many times as needed.
constraints: 1 <= length of each word in wordDict <= 20
s and the words in wordDict consist of lowercase English letters only
all the words in wordDict are distinct
notes: s is exactly equal to a single dictionary word
a greedy split from the left fails, but a different split succeeds (like 'catsandog')
s requires reusing the same word more than once

sampleTestCases.explanation: "leetcode" splits into "leet" + "code", both in the dictionary

sampleTestCases.input: s = "catsandog", wordDict = "cats dog sand and cat"
sampleTestCases.explanation: every way of splitting the prefix leaves a trailing chunk that isn't a dictionary word

optimal.time: O(n^2) using an O(1)-ish substring/hash lookup per split point, where n is s.length
optimal.space: O(n) for the breakable array, plus a hash set for the dictionary words
optimal.pattern: dynamic programming - let breakable(i) mean the prefix s[0:i] can be fully split into dictionary words

bruteForce.approach: recursively try every prefix of the remaining string that matches a dictionary word, and recurse on the rest; return true if any path consumes the whole string
bruteForce.time: O(2^n) - exponential, recomputes the same suffixes repeatedly
